components.rationale: Body 15-26 states, for 0<=p_m<1, prod(1-p_m)>0 iff sum p_m<inf (the negation-equivalent form of source Ex. 4.3.4, prod=0 iff sum=inf), with the product defined as the decreasing limit of finite products. Annex 4-30 writes both Borel-Cantelli directions on independent uniforms with A_m={U_m<=p_m}: P(A_m)=p_m, independence and continuity give the limit formula (6-12); the second lemma gives probability zero when the sum diverges (13-15); the first lemma gives a positive-probability tail event T_N, and block independence gives the positive product, with p_m<1 used for the positive initial factors (17-27). Route results used are proved theorems: thm:p15-borel-cantelli-first and thm:p15-borel-cantelli-second, thm:p15-independent-sequence-existence, thm:p15-independent-blocks. Source p.233: the hypothesis p_m in [0,1), both directions and the Borel-Cantelli route all match.

Body 28-45 defines D_n, treats the zero finite-survival case, defines hazards h_n=P(A_n|D_{n-1}) in [0,1), and states P(D_n)=P(A_1^c)prod(1-h_j) and P(no A_j)=0 iff sum h_j=inf with no independence assumption. Annex 32-51 writes the containment argument for the zero case, the conditional-probability recursion, h_n<1 from positivity, iteration, continuity along decreasing D_n, and application of the event-product criterion to h_2,h_3,... Source p.234 Ex. 4.3.5 (divergent sum of conditional hazards implies zero probability that no A_m occurs) is the if-direction of the stated equivalence; the source's implicit positivity of the conditioning events is covered by the explicit zero-survival case.

Body 49-62 defines elementary conditional averages over finite refining partitions, with zero on null cells, and claims measurability, integrability and the integral identity on every event of F_n. Annex 55-61 proves integrability by the cell bound and the all-event identity by cell integration and finite addition, with null cells handled. This supplies the source's closing remark in Ex. 4.3.7 (p.234) that the conditional expectations needed for Example 4.3.7 have elementary definitions, and gives meaning to E(X_{n+1}|F_n) in Ex. 4.3.6.

source_evidence.item: Exercise 4.3.7 non-circularity remark; Exercise 4.3.6 conditional expectation

components.rationale: Body 64-83: ratio process X_n=mu(I)/nu(I) with zero on nu-null cells; X_n>=0, E X_n<=mu(Omega), the supermartingale inequality for elementary averages; equality, martingale property and constant integral under local absolute continuity; a strict-loss example. Annex 63-85 writes the total-integral computation, the child-cell computation for a positive parent cell, equality when every omitted null child has zero mu-mass, restoration of the total mass, the null-parent case, and the example's values (X_0=1, later X_n=0). Source p.234 Ex. 4.3.6 (direct check of the martingale property; supermartingale inequality after dropping mu_n<<nu_n and setting X_n=0 on nu-null cells), in the Example 4.3.7 setting of p.229 (refining partitions indexed 0<=k<K_n, finite mu, probability nu), matches both parts.

Body 85-93 states the bounded convergence lemma for elementary martingales on refining finite partitions. Annex 89-122 writes the M=0 case; predictable 0/1 holdings constant on F_{j-1} cells; E G_N=0 from the elementary mean identity on each cell; the pathwise bound (b-a)U_N<=G_N+(a-Y_N)^+ for completed and unfinished trades; E U_N<=M/(b-a); monotone convergence; the countable rational-pair argument for almost-sure convergence in [0,M]; the measurable limit; and dominated convergence for L^1. No general conditional expectation or Radon-Nikodym representation is used. This supplies the convergence of the bounded martingales that source Ex. 4.3.7 obtains by applying Theorem 4.3.5 (pp.227-228), in the elementary form the exercise's remark requires.

source_evidence.item: Theorem 4.3.5 proof: bounded martingales Y_n, Z_n with limits

components.rationale: Body 95-110: F countably generated, sigma-finite mu<<nu, a nonnegative measurable f with mu(A)=int_A f dnu, unique and finite nu-a.e., built from finite partitions and the elementary lemma. Annex 126-211 writes the finite/probability case: rho=(mu+nu)/(c+1), Boolean-atom partitions that refine and generate F, bounded ratios Y_n and Z_n with Y_n+Z_n=c+1, exact martingale identities, the elementary convergence lemma, int_A Y drho=mu(A) on the generating algebra and pi-system uniqueness, nu(Z=0)=0 and rho(Z=0)=0, f=Y/Z, the change-of-measure identity, the c=0 case, and f identified as the limit of the Example 4.3.7 ratios X_n=Y_n/Z_n. It writes the sigma-finite assembly: a common countable partition D_i of finite mass under both measures, null blocks, normalized local probabilities, gluing and summation over blocks, and finiteness a.e. It writes uniqueness through the sets A_{i,k}. The trace-generation step (178-182) is an instance of thm:p15-measurability-criterion (generated preimages) for the inclusion map. The uniqueness step is thm:p15-measure-uniqueness. Source p.234 Ex. 4.3.7: the countably generated hypothesis, sigma-finite mu and nu, mu<<nu, existence of g, and the non-circularity remark all match (body 9-11, definition 61, annex 120-121 and 154-155). The Theorem 4.3.5 route of pp.227-229 (mixture reference, Y=dmu/drho, Z=dnu/drho, X=Y/Z) is reproduced in elementary form.

Body 114-128 defines mu and nu as products of Bernoulli(alpha_m) and Bernoulli(beta_m) for alpha_m,beta_m in [0,1] on binary sequence space, with coordinates xi_m and affinity a_m in [0,1], and records the real-sequence-space realization that lets the real-coordinate product theorem apply. The bound a_m<=1 follows from the square identity 2(1-a_m)=(sqrt alpha_m - sqrt beta_m)^2+(sqrt(1-alpha_m)-sqrt(1-beta_m))^2, written at annex 290-294. Source p.234 Bernoulli preamble (F_n,G_n concentrated on {0,1}, F_n(0)=1-alpha_n, G_n(0)=1-beta_n) matches, with mu paired to alpha and nu to beta, as in the source.

Body 130-158 states the full criterion (mu<<nu iff local support and prod a_m>0), positivity of each a_m and the equivalent condition sum(1-a_m)<inf, the epsilon-regime quadratic bounds, equivalence iff sum(alpha-beta)^2<inf with singularity otherwise, and labels the endpoint criterion an extension of the source. Annex 216-253 writes these steps. Necessity of local support follows from coordinate pushforwards. Local support gives coordinate absolute continuity. The square-root density integral equals a_m, including reference-null points. thm:p15-product-affinity-criterion, which allows zero coordinate densities, gives both directions. thm:p15-product-affinity-series gives the sum form, and thm:p15-product-density-filtration (annex 193-204) supplies positivity of each affinity. The annex also writes the exact square identity, the denominator bounds 4eps to 4(1-eps), the quadratic bounds, and equivalence or singularity in the regime. Source p.234 Ex. 4.3.8: (i) a necessary and sufficient condition via Theorem 4.3.8 (pp.229-230), whose standing positivity assumption q_n>0 is extended rather than narrowed; (ii) for 0<eps<=alpha_n,beta_n<=1-eps<1 the condition is sum(alpha_n-beta_n)^2<inf. Both parts match.

Body 160-171 and annex 257-277 write the singularity proof: for the tail event F of finitely many successes, the first Borel-Cantelli lemma gives mu(F)=1, and independence with the second lemma gives nu(F)=0. They also write the explicit example alpha_m=(m+1)^-2, beta_m=(m+1)^-1: it is interior, satisfies sum(alpha-beta)^2<=sum beta^2<inf via 0<beta_m-alpha_m<beta_m, and is singular. So the interior bound in the quadratic criterion cannot be dropped. Source p.234 Ex. 4.3.9 hypothesis (sum alpha_n<inf, sum beta_n=inf), the conclusion mu perp nu, and the claim that sum(alpha_n-beta_n)^2<inf is not sufficient for mu<<nu in general all match, with an explicit witness supplied.

Body 173-186 and annex 282-313 prove (sqrt x - sqrt y)^2<=|x-y|, including the both-zero case, and 2(1-a_m)<=2|alpha_m-beta_m|, so the affinity deviations are summable. Under local support the affinities are positive, and the complete criterion gives mu<<nu. For interior probabilities the reverse local condition holds, which gives mutual absolute continuity. They also give the counterexample for failed local support (a_1=1/sqrt2, the cylinder {xi_1=1}) and prove it is not singular, via the measure nu/2 dominated by both. Source p.234 Ex. 4.3.10 (0<alpha_n,beta_n<1, sum|alpha_n-beta_n|<inf sufficient for mu<<nu without the epsilon bound) matches.

The proof boundary (body 188-196) and the chapter scope (body 5-11) claim that every one of Exercises 4.3.4-4.3.10 is supplied with its own route. The event product uses Borel-Cantelli (annex 4-30). The density uses finite partitions and elementary upcrossings (annex 53-212). The Bernoulli comparisons use the full affinity criterion and a separate event-occurrence counterexample (annex 215-315). Item-by-item comparison with source pp.233-234 confirms the claim: 4.3.4 -> C001, 4.3.5 -> C002, 4.3.6 -> C004, 4.3.7 -> C003/C005/C006, the preamble -> C007, 4.3.8 -> C008, 4.3.9 -> C009, 4.3.10 -> C010. No exercise, hypothesis, case, example or justificatory remark of 4.3.4-4.3.10 is missing.
